job is to commit to a concrete model identifier and its hyperparameters.

## Plan

{
  "strategy": "Attempt 4: refit the best-known ranking (iteration 2's heavily regularised hist_gbdt with impute 'none') and change exactly one lever — the class weight — from 'balanced' (which pins the positive weight at ~5.07) to an explicit {\\\"0\\\": 1, \\\"1\\\": 6.5}, pushing the default predict() cut a little further toward recall so recall (0.7355) and specificity (0.8200) meet near the point where balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut (0.7891) is realised. Everything else is held byte-identical to iteration 2: max_iter 600, learning_rate 0.03, max_leaf_nodes 8, max_depth 4, min_samples_leaf 60, l2_regularization 20.0, max_features 0.6, early_stopping false so all 5,026 train rows are fitted, and preprocessing impute 'none' / no scaling / no missingness columns so the trees keep splitting on NaN natively across the 60 missing columns (expected_num_interested_in_me at 78.5%). Read the row as an operating-point-only move: roc_auc / pr_auc / balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut should stay within noise of 0.8604 / 0.5925 / 0.7891, and any balanced_accuracy change is the cut. cut_headroom of 0.0113 caps what this can buy, so this attempt is about converting the last measurable piece of the operating point, not about clearing the 0.8882 bar — which lies 0.099 above the best ranking ceiling this column set has produced across two families.",

  },

    "impute": "none",

    "missing_indicator": false,
    "missing_count": false
  },
  "changes_from_last": "Differs from iteration 3 (extra_trees, median impute, missing_count true) by returning to hist_gbdt with impute 'none' and no added missingness column. Differs from iteration 2 — the configuration it otherwise reproduces — in exactly one key: class_weight goes from 'balanced' (implicit positive weight ≈5.07) to the explicit map {\"0\": 1, \"1\": 6.5}. Differs from iteration 1 in capacity<path> (600 iters at lr 0.03, 8 leaves, depth 4, leaf 60, l2 20, max_features 0.6) as well as in the weight. No previous attempt has used an explicit class-weight map, so this is a new point in the run.",
  "rationale": "The two axes read apart: the ranking axis has plateaued (balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut 0.7922 → 0.7891 → 0.7715 across gbdt and bagging, a span of 0.0207) while the bar at 0.8882 sits 0.099 above the best of those, so no remaining lever on this column set covers it; the honest remaining purchase is the operating point, where cut_headroom is 0.0113 on the best row. class_weight is the only lever the executor exposes for that axis, and 'balanced' is one point on it rather than the optimum — it fixes the positive weight at the class frequency 5.07, and at that point recall 0.7355 still trails specificity 0.8200, meaning the default cut sits on the conservative side of the balanced-accuracy-maximising cut. Raising the positive weight modestly to 6.5 (about 28% above 'balanced', a small step so it does not overshoot into recall≫specificity) should move recall up and specificity down until they meet, recovering most of the 0.0113. Holding capacity, regularisation and preprocessing byte-identical to iteration 2 keeps the row attributable: if roc_auc and balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut stay flat and balanced_accuracy moves, the movement is unambiguously the cut. Capacity is not the constraint any more (train_val_gap fell 0.2752 → 0.1036 with train_balanced_accuracy 0.8813, so no memorisation to fix), and cost is trivial (8.4 s of the 600 s budget), so nothing is resource-bound. Expected outcome ≈0.785–0.789 balanced_accuracy — a small resolved gain over 0.7778 and a defensible best row, with the bar itself out of reach for these columns.",
